selection_rule: top-k species by (n_distinct_proposers, n_members, stable sha256); representative = member with smallest sha256(pid)

species_table.rep_name: States core position in opening sentences

Share of the text that is new information rather than restatement

Quantitative content that bears on the specific choice before the agency

Textual defect located together with operable replacement language
Engages the agency's stated rationale, and represents the proposal faithfully

Scan and attachment debris: OCR corruption, stubs, stray headers

Supplied campaign wording and stock talking points

selected.name: Pinpoint statutory/regulatory citation
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment cites specific statutory sections, CFR provisions, or exact regulatory text (by number/subsection) that are relevant and appear accurately applied to the argument. A 10: multiple precise, correctly-used pinpoint citations integrated into the argument. A 0: no statutory/regulatory citations, or only vague references to 'the law' or 'the Act' without section numbers.
selected.rationale: R25 (State of Colorado, dense_pct=0.898, card_pct=0.038) cites 33 U.S.C. sections 1251(b), 1341, and 1370 by number, and R09 (Eversheds Sutherland, dense_pct=0.881, card_pct=0.211) cites the exact proposed Treas. Reg. section at issue -- both dense_high_card_low, with dense ranking near the top of the pool for this legal precision while the scorecard ranks both near the bottom.
member_names: Analyzes who the rule as written would advantage, and by what mechanism
Pinpoint statutory or regulatory authority challenge
Situates the proposal in the history of the rules it would change

selected.name: Alternative comparison
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the comment compares the proposal with one or more concrete alternatives using explicit advantages, disadvantages, or applicability conditions; score 0 when it supplies no alternative or merely demands rejection.
selected.rationale: R01 proposes adaptive oversight, internal expertise, and user-fee resources, while R08 explains why a rearview mirror may be unnecessary for autonomous vehicles and R50 compares future-commitment reporting with shipment reporting.
member_names: Argument stands on its own text rather than on affiliation or deferral
Differentiated position with a distinct reason on each side
Takes a position the agency can act on rather than requesting clarification

selected.name: Causal impact pathway
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the comment clearly traces how a proposed provision produces specific operational, economic, safety, health, or environmental effects; score 0 when it asserts harm or benefit without explaining the mechanism.
selected.rationale: R02 connects the proposed TCE prohibition to qualified aerospace processes and transition constraints, while R39 traces renewable-fuel rules through RIN prices, refiners, workers, and consumers.

selected.name: Uncertainty calibration
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes established facts, uncertainty, incomplete information, assumptions, and speculation; score 0 when it presents uncertain or unsupported claims as settled facts.
selected.rationale: R14 explicitly identifies incomplete population surveys and challenges an overconfident conclusion, while R19 separates reported temperature findings from its tentative storm hypothesis.

selected.name: First-hand operational evidence for claims
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment's claims are grounded in the filer's own direct first-hand operational, technical, or field experience (their own fleet, lab, cases, data) rather than generic policy assertions. A 10: comment clearly draws on specific first-hand experience the filer possesses and describes it concretely. A 0: comment consists entirely of generic assertions with no indication of direct first-hand experience.
selected.rationale: R02 (Japan Airlines, dense_pct=0.139, card_pct=0.918) grounds its argument in JAL's own actuator-installation timeline experience, and R34 (a USGS biologist's peer-review email on the Iiwi status report, dense_pct=0.080, card_pct=0.724) cites specific field studies and corrects specific sentences from direct expertise -- both dense_low_card_high, with dense ranking both near the very bottom of the pool despite the scorecard recognizing their substance, suggesting dense may discount genuine first-hand expertise when it arrives in an unpolished or informal register (a technical bulletin excerpt; a casual email) rather than formal advocacy prose.
member_names: First-hand operational or casework facts the agency does not already have

selected.name: Relevant experiential expertise
selected.instruction: Score 10 when the commenter’s role or direct experience is explicitly connected to a concrete, docket-specific observation; score 0 when credentials or affiliation appear only as generic self-description.
selected.rationale: R16 connects dermatologists’ clinical experience to prior authorization barriers, and R40 connects tribal transportation program experience to administrative and community needs.

selected.name: Substantive signal density
selected.instruction: Score 10 when most of the text contributes new, proposal-specific analysis with little repetition or boilerplate; score 0 when the text is dominated by pleasantries, credentials, generic endorsement, repetition, or irrelevant material.
selected.rationale: R18, R22, R37, and R50 devote substantial space to analysis, while R05, R21, and R46 contain relatively little beyond affiliation and general support.
member_names: Substantive payload relative to length and formality

selected.name: Evidence traceability
selected.instruction: Score 10 when claims are tied to identifiable studies, statutes, datasets, reports, or other sources and the sources are meaningfully interpreted; score 0 when citations are absent, vague, or merely decorative.
selected.rationale: R03, R19, R24, and R26 integrate named evidence into their reasoning, whereas R15 and R55 make factual assertions with limited source traceability.

selected.name: States core position in opening sentences
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment's central request or position (support/oppose/specific ask) is clearly stated within the first two sentences, versus deferred behind extended preamble or organizational background. A 10: the specific ask or position is unambiguous from the first sentence or two. A 0: the reader must read through substantial preamble before the core position becomes clear.
selected.rationale: R08 (ACC extension request, dense_pct=0.079, card_pct=0.830) opens by stating the exact 30-day extension request in its first line, and R39 (coral habitat comment, dense_pct=0.197, card_pct=0.793) opens 'I strongly SUPPORT...' as its first sentence -- both dense_low_card_high, with the scorecard rewarding this immediacy far above where dense ranks it.
member_names: States core position in opening sentences

selected.name: Concrete organizational standing disclosed
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter establishes concrete, verifiable standing relevant to the rule -- membership size, statutory mandate, years of operation, or domain expertise -- beyond a bare assertion of interest. A 10: comment states specific, concrete standing facts directly tied to the rule's subject. A 0: the commenter's relationship to and authority on the subject matter is entirely unstated or purely generic ('as a concerned citizen').
selected.rationale: R55 (NASW, dense_pct=0.801, card_pct=0.134) opens by stating '130,000 members' and its role in LTC advocacy, and R14 (ASSE, dense_pct=0.965, card_pct=0.255) states '37,000... safety, health, and environmental professionals' -- both dense_high_card_low, suggesting dense rewards this credentialing far more than the scorecard does.

selected.name: Claims calibrated to evidence, no leaps
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the strength of the comment's claims matches the strength of its evidence, avoiding unsupported causal leaps, conspiratorial framing, or sweeping conclusions drawn from a single tangential fact. A 10: every claim is proportionate to and follows logically from the evidence offered. A 0: comment draws sweeping or conspiratorial conclusions (e.g., alleging a coordinated cover-up, or linking an isolated local fact to a global causal claim) without supporting logic.
selected.rationale: R43 (dense_pct=0.383, card_pct=0.925) leaps from one volcano's CO2 output and an unnamed 'group of German scientists' to dismissing anthropogenic climate policy entirely, and R49 (dense_pct=0.264, card_pct=0.908) asserts a coordinated 'fake govt study' conspiracy without evidence -- both dense_low_card_high, with the scorecard rating both extremely high despite the reasoning failures dense (correctly) discounts.
member_names: Claims calibrated to evidence, no leaps

selected.name: Acknowledges both merits and drawbacks
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explicitly identifies both positive and negative aspects of the proposal (or explicitly frames the regulator's own competing goals) rather than arguing one-sidedly. A 10: comment clearly separates what it supports from what it opposes and explains why for each. A 0: comment is purely one-sided (all praise or all condemnation) with no acknowledgment of any countervailing consideration.
selected.rationale: R05 (U.S. Chamber of Commerce, dense_pct=0.708, card_pct=0.100) explicitly separates 'positive developments' it welcomes from 'problematic provisions' it opposes, and R06 (Alliance for Automotive Innovation, dense_pct=0.878, card_pct=0.115) frames Congress's own balancing of competing goals before taking a position -- both dense_high_card_low, suggesting balanced argumentation is exactly the property the scorecard is missing.

selected.name: Internally consistent, labeled quantitative detail
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether numeric figures in the comment (dollar amounts, dates, volumes, percentages, thresholds) are clearly labeled, tied to a specific claim, and internally consistent with each other, versus numbers appearing without clear labels or context. A 10: every number is clearly labeled, its meaning is unambiguous, and figures are internally consistent. A 0: numbers appear disconnected from any clear label or claim, making it impossible to tell what they refer to or whether they are consistent.
selected.rationale: R51 (Monroe Energy, dense_pct=0.939, card_pct=0.157, dense_high_card_low) ties every figure ('13.8 billion gallons,' '390 million gallons,' '1.2 billion gallons') to a specific, clearly-labeled ask, which the scorecard entirely fails to reward. R12 (dense_pct=0.804, card_pct=0.128, dense_high_card_low) is a dense wall of dollar figures and percentages stripped of labels by OCR extraction, uninterpretable as presented -- dense rates it almost as highly as R51's cleanly-labeled figures, suggesting dense may be responding to the surface presence of quantitative data without verifying it is actually interpretable, a distinction this criterion would sharpen.

selected.name: Substance-to-boilerplate ratio
selected.instruction: Score 0-10 on what fraction of the visible text is actual argument/analysis versus non-substantive administrative content (letterhead, attorney/board rosters, address blocks, signature blocks, 'see attached file' notices). A 10: virtually all text is substantive argument. A 0: the great majority of visible text is letterhead, personnel lists, or contact boilerplate with little or no argument.
selected.rationale: R03 (Sonosky law firm letter, dense_pct=0.970, card_pct=0.188) and R14 (ASSE letter, dense_pct=0.965, card_pct=0.255) are both dense_high_card_low: extensive attorney rosters and board-of-directors lists dominate the visible text before any argument appears, yet dense rates both near the top of the pool while the scorecard rates both near the bottom -- suggesting dense credits the institutional apparatus that the scorecard discounts (or fails to see past).

selected.name: Share of the text that is new information rather than restatement
selected.instruction: Estimate what fraction of the comment's substance is content the agency did not already possess. 10 = nearly all of it: argument, data, experience, or drafting the agency could not have written for itself. 5 = roughly half restatement of the proposal, half addition. 0 = a faithful summary of the proposal, or of another commenter's position, followed by agreement or disagreement, adding nothing. Length must not earn credit; a long, accurate, well-organized paraphrase belongs at the bottom of this scale.
selected.rationale: R56 reproduces the proposed trip limits, seasons, and allocations species by species and appends agreement to each. R39 restates what the AD would require and then supports it. R13 states only that the commenter concurs with the board president's and vice president's comments. All three are dense_low_card_high, and the first two are long and orderly while contributing nothing the agency did not write itself. The high end is R19, which contributes four specific requested actions including a mechanism -- a government-issued RIN available when RIN prices are too high -- that appears nowhere in the proposal.
member_names: Share of the text that is new information rather than restatement

selected.name: OCR and typographical noise
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much visible OCR corruption, misspelling, character substitution, spacing error, broken formatting, or typographical noise appears? Score only the amount of noise, not the writer's competence or the comment's quality.
selected.rationale: R08, R42, and R54 contain conspicuous scanning or transcription artifacts, while R12 contains many spelling and spacing errors; these surface defects can affect text processing without reflecting substantive merit.
member_names: OCR/scan transcription artifacts and garbled text
upstream_parent_all_members: age of original document / scanning-pipeline artifact

selected.name: Footnote and formal legal-citation density
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate how much the text uses formal legal-citation apparatus -- numbered footnotes, and/or pin-cites to statutes, regulations, or the Federal Register (e.g. 'U.S.C.', 'C.F.R.', 'Fed. Reg.'). 0 = no such citations or footnotes, 10 = dense, extensive footnoting/citation throughout. Do NOT judge whether the citations are accurate or persuasive -- score only the extent of the citation apparatus present.
selected.rationale: Footnote/citation density is concentrated in dense-favored organizational filings: R14 (NHA, footnotes 1-2 with Fed. Reg. pin-cites), R33 (NASW, three numbered footnotes citing prior letters), R55 (Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids, footnotes 1-3 citing NSDUH data). This tracks professional drafting convention, not argument strength.
member_names: Legal-authority citation apparatus: statutes, Federal Register cites, footnotes
selected.upstream_parent: professional editing / legal training of drafter
upstream_parent_all_members: drafting by trained legal counsel (outside law firm or in-house regulatory lawyers) rather than by the affected party directly
professional editing / legal training of drafter

selected.name: Typographic emphasis intensity (all-caps, exclamation marks)
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate how much the text uses typographic emphasis markers -- words in ALL CAPS, exclamation points, or repeated emphatic punctuation -- to convey urgency or emotion. 0 = no such emphasis markers, 10 = frequent and heavy use throughout. Do NOT judge whether the emotional tone is appropriate or persuasive -- score only the extent of the typographic emphasis markers.
selected.rationale: Typographic emphasis appears mostly in card-favored personal comments: R01 uses 'strongly SUPPORT' in caps, R25 repeats 'EVERYONE' and 'SO MANY' in caps, and R45 is written almost entirely in emphatic, run-on caps-laden prose. This is a register/affect marker, not a quality marker.

selected.name: Sender authority cues
selected.instruction: How much does the text display senior titles, professional credentials, official roles, or named authoritative representatives? Score only their visible extent, not whether the authority makes the comment good.
selected.rationale: The upstream factor is sender seniority; its fingerprint is titles and credentials such as Governor, Executive Director, Staff Engineer, or designated representative. Examples include R10, R11, R33, and R59. Authority cues may affect reception independently of argument quality.

selected.name: Coordinated template language
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text show stock, coalition, endorsement, or template language, including references to other comments, shared positions, or attached submissions? Score only textual recurrence or coordination signals, not whether the position is good.
selected.rationale: R11, R19, and R32 explicitly echo or endorse positions associated with larger organizations; such coordination can affect reception while being separate from the individual text's substantive quality.
member_names: Coalition or third-party endorsement / 'joined by' language

selected.name: Procedural-only request (extension, scheduling, logistics)
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, rate how much the comment's content is a purely procedural request -- e.g. a request to extend the comment period, a scheduling or logistics question, or a request for clarification about process -- rather than substantive engagement with the rule's provisions. 0 = comment is entirely substantive engagement with the rule's merits, 10 = comment is entirely a procedural request with no substantive engagement. Do NOT judge whether the procedural request is reasonable or well-justified -- score only the extent to which the content is procedural rather than substantive.
selected.rationale: Some items are purely procedural and never engage the rule's merits: R17 (ACC/CBC's entire text is a 30-day extension request) and R54 (Philip Morris's entire text is a 90-day extension request); R56 (ALPA's one-line 'IN SUPPORT' AD comment) is similarly minimal engagement. Whether a comment is procedural-only is a strong, easily-scored predictor independent of substantive quality.
member_names: Process-management asks about the rulemaking's conduct, not its content
selected.upstream_parent: submission-timing pressure on the commenter's internal review process
upstream_parent_all_members: submission-timing pressure on the commenter's internal review process
when in the docket's life the item was produced and filed (an early, deadline-driven procedural filing vs. a later substantive one), and the filer's familiarity with docket mechanics

selected.name: Personal-experience framing
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much does the text present the writer's personal circumstances, family, occupation, identity, location, or direct lived experience? Score only the extent of self-reference, not whether the experience strengthens the comment.
selected.rationale: Personal framing is prominent in R03, R09, and R33, whereas many institutional submissions suppress it; this may track author position or access while sometimes also contributing genuine substance.
selected.upstream_parent: author role and access to lived experience
upstream_parent_all_members: author role and access to lived experience

selected.name: Sheer volume of retained body text
selected.instruction: Reading only the comment text, score 0-10 for HOW MUCH body text there is, as a raw quantity. Judge extent by approximate word count and by structural signs of length: numbered or lettered section headings, a table of contents, roman-numeral parts, bulleted lists of asks, and page-continuation markers. Anchors: 0 = under roughly 60 words (one short paragraph); 3 = a few paragraphs; 5 = roughly one page; 8 = several pages with internal sectioning; 10 = a long multi-part document with a contents listing or many numbered sections. Do NOT reward or penalise length, do NOT judge whether the length is warranted by the subject, and do NOT consider how well the space is used. Report volume only.
selected.rationale: MODE 1 counter with a MODE 2 parent. Length is the canonical nuisance: it is cheap for a resourced filer and expensive for an individual, and it separates the two halves of this slice almost mechanically. R12 (about 50 words) and R46 (two sentences) are dense_low_card_high; R29 (State of Colorado, multi-page with statutory sections), R52 (Monroe Energy, with an EXECUTIVE SUMMARY and bulleted asks) and R13 (which literally opens with a 'Contents ... Transcript ... List of Attendees' listing) are long documents on the dense_high_card_low side. Tagged mixed honestly: more preparation time plausibly buys genuine substance as well as bulk, so this must appear in the sensitivity band rather than being silently discounted.
member_names: Sheer volume of retained body text
selected.upstream_parent: staff time and preparation resources invested in the submission (in-house counsel, consultants, an organization drafting over weeks vs. an individual typing at a keyboard)
upstream_parent_all_members: institutional resources / staff time available to draft
staff time and preparation resources invested in the submission (in-house counsel, consultants, an organization drafting over weeks vs. an individual typing at a keyboard)

selected.name: Text volume
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much text volume is present, measured by visible length, pages, paragraphs, subpoints, or extended elaboration? Score only quantity, not whether the additional text is useful or well reasoned.
selected.rationale: The very short comments in R03 and R06 contrast with the lengthy submissions in R10 and R46; sheer volume can predict model treatment without being a quality attribute.

selected.name: Submission apparatus
selected.instruction: On a 0-10 scale, how much formal submission apparatus is visible, including letterhead, postal addresses, docket metadata, named officials, contact details, transmission methods, page headers, and signatures? Score only extent of apparatus, not professionalism or quality.
selected.rationale: The elaborate filing apparatus in R04, R43, and R60 may reflect organizational administrative capacity and docket familiarity, which can influence visibility independently of the arguments themselves.
selected.upstream_parent: institutional submission infrastructure and process familiarity
upstream_parent_all_members: institutional submission infrastructure and process familiarity
